transfers.from: signal_noise: Signal and Noise in a Budget-Limited Coding Agent (Almarwani); full write-up read by the reader agent
transfers.idea: The write-up's adapter passed a pre-registered held-out likelihood gate (+0.0142 nats per token against a threshold of +0.01; 17 of 19 tasks improved) and then solved the same number of tasks as the base model (15 of 36 each). A post hoc split showed why: 10 of 133 held-out steps, holding 20.8% of the scored tokens (closing messages without a tool call), carried 85.1% of the gain. The project's reader is the same kind of average. The next direction, the RSI share and the gain all come from the mean block-14 state over every continuation token, and such a mean can be dominated by a small token class that is not the one of interest: explicit RSI keywords (the RSI share would then be a keyword echo) or layout tokens (the shared style direction would then be a formatting attractor). The outside probe's foreign-word effect may likewise sit in a few words or positions.
transfers.concrete_measurement: Re-read the stored round-1 texts with the unpushed model and keep per-token block-14 states, centred on the grand mean over all tokens of both arms. For each round and each axis a (RSI axis, converged style direction, each foreign axis) the contribution of token t in text i is (h_it - mean) . a / (T_i N), positive for pro texts and negative for anti texts; these sum exactly to the projection of the next direction on a. Group tokens into classes fixed in writing beforehand: (1) tokens of the RSI word list, (2) the first 8 continuation tokens, (3) punctuation, newline and list-format tokens, (4) end-of-text and boilerplate, (5) other content tokens. Report per class the share of tokens and the signed share of the projection, round by round, with a bootstrap interval over prompts. Add one counterfactual: replace the RSI-list tokens in the texts with neutral placeholders, re-read, and measure how much of the RSI projection disappears. For the outside probe, split the foreign-word log-probability gain by word and by position and give the share of the three largest words and a leave-one-word-out range. Reading rules: if class 1 or the placeholder test accounts for most of the RSI projection, the RSI share is lexical and its decay should track the keyword count per text; if class 3 accounts for most of the style projection, the shared direction is a layout attractor; if the positive control's signal sits in a small class, round 1b should use a class-restricted reader, defined on one half of the prompts and tested on the other.
transfers.cost: Forward passes over stored texts, no generation: well under one GPU-hour on a 1.7B model, plus about a day of analysis code. If the round-1 texts were not stored, one rerun of round 1.
transfers.risk: The classes are chosen after round 1 has been seen, the weakness the write-up's author concedes for his own split; writing them down first and cross-fitting limits it. A block-14 state already mixes earlier tokens through attention, so position-based shares understate lexical influence; the placeholder re-read checks this, but edited texts are slightly off-distribution.

transfers.from: signal_noise: Signal and Noise in a Budget-Limited Coding Agent (Almarwani); full write-up read by the reader agent
transfers.idea: The write-up reruns identical archives to obtain a noise floor (8 of 71 tasks flip between two identical local runs; the same bytes score 0.13 to 0.20 on the public board), judges every contrast against it (of 48 paired configuration contrasts none survives Holm correction) and reports its adapter's 15 against 15 of 36 as 'no detectable change', not as zero effect. The project's indicators are functions of a noisy estimate, because each next direction is a mean difference over a finite number of sampled texts. Two consequences follow. A gain computed from the norm of that difference has a positive floor, the norm tau of its sampling error, even with no transmission (a gain computed as projection on the pushed direction does not). And every cosine with a fixed axis is shrunk by the square root of the direction's reliability. If the response shrinks over rounds, reliability shrinks with it, so part of the observed decay of the RSI share can be attenuation by noise.
transfers.concrete_measurement: (a) From per-text reader states, per round: split the prompts into halves 200 times, compute the direction from each half, take the mean split-half cosine rho and the reliability r = 2 rho / (1 + rho) of the full-sample direction (equivalently r = 1 - tau^2 / |m|^2, with m the mean pro-minus-anti difference). Report the debiased response sqrt(max(|m|^2 - tau^2, 0)) per unit push and the RSI cosine divided by sqrt(r times r_axis), where r_axis is the same reliability for the RSI axis. (b) Rerun 3 to 5 identical loops (same start, prompts, alpha, temperature; different sampling seeds) and record per round the spread of RSI cosine, gain, damage and persona log-odds and the cosine between replicate loops. Criteria: the RSI decay counts only if the corrected cosine falls by more than the replicate spread. Convergence to a shared style direction counts if loops from different starts are as similar to each other as replicates of one start. Every round-2 contrast (phase-diagram cells, counter-steering against the foreign-axis control) is judged against the replicate spread, with Holm correction over a family of contrasts named beforehand. Null claims ('behaviour does not move', 'foreign effect about zero') are stated against a margin fixed in advance: zero within the margin if the 90% interval lies inside it, otherwise inconclusive.
transfers.cost: (a) is analysis only if per-text mean states were stored, otherwise one re-read of stored texts. (b) costs 3 to 5 times one loop configuration and fits into round 2 as extra seeds.
transfers.risk: The correction is unstable at low reliability (below about 0.2, report 'not resolvable'). Splits must be by prompt if pro and anti texts share prompts. Noise lying along the RSI axis biases the correction. Seed replicates say nothing about dependence on the prompt set. Margins are a judgement call and must be written down before the data are seen.

transfers.from: neuron_engineering: Synthetic Neuron Engineering of a Gemma 4 Coding Agent (Taneja); full paper read by the reader agent
transfers.idea: A forced 'quote exactly' sentence at the start of the model's reasoning changed behaviour in context (the edit applied at 221 of 461 moments, against 153 with nothing and 159 with a neutral sentence). The same sentence's effect, written into the output weights of one layer as a rank-128 least-squares change (layer 10 or 14), did nothing (147 and 135, against 141 unchanged and 163 for the control). An effect that exists in context need not be reproducible by an additive change at one depth. Round 1's finding that behaviour on held-out statements does not move may reflect the same limit: block 14 alone may not carry enough of a persona's effect at the statement positions, whichever direction is pushed. The write-up also supplies the scale the project lacks, the share of a log-probability gap closed, reported beside damage and beside a strict count of flipped preferences (57% closed at 9% damage, yet only 6 of 25 cases flipped against 3 at baseline).
transfers.concrete_measurement: For each held-out persona statement run the model with an explicit RSI persona instruction and with a neutral instruction of equal token length (so positions align). G is the resulting difference in log-odds. (1) Copy the block-14 residual states at all positions after the instruction from the instructed run into the neutral run and measure the share of G recovered: the ceiling for any on-distribution intervention at block 14. (2) Push the mean instructed-minus-neutral block-14 difference as one direction at the standard push size and measure the share of G recovered. (3) Repeat (1) at blocks 6, 10, 18 and 22. (4) Re-express the round-1 behavioural result, and later every direction at several push sizes, as share of G closed beside damage (KL to the unpushed model) and the number of statements whose sign flips. Reading rules: if (1) recovers little (say under a third), the round-1 behavioural null is uninformative about the loop and (3) should choose the injection block; if (1) is high and (2) low, the persona effect is not one additive direction; if (2) is high while the RSI axis and loop directions stay near zero, report their cosines with the instruction direction, since they then lack the component that drives behaviour.
transfers.cost: Forward passes with hooks: statements times two conditions times five blocks, well under one GPU-hour. Step (4) on round-1 data is analysis only.
transfers.risk: Patching whole states carries over everything that differs between the two prompts, so sufficiency can be overstated; the equal-length neutral instruction limits this. The ceiling holds for the positions patched; a push applied at every position during generation is a different intervention. Even the in-context sentence in the write-up did not improve the final outcome (the real fix was reproduced 26 against 25 times of 281), so G is a proxy scale, not proof of behavioural relevance.

transfers.from: last_mile_copy: The Last Mile Is a Copy (Shree); full write-up read by the reader agent, figures and supplementary notebook not
transfers.idea: In the write-up a difference-of-means direction in MLP activations separated invented from correctly copied edits with AUC 0.81, yet projecting it out did not repair copying (9 to 11% rescued, against 13% for the unmodified model in that run): detection without correction. The reader agent notes that the AUC has no interval and the projection no random-direction control. Round 2 counter-steers and ablates directions of the same kind, since the RSI axis is a difference of means. An ablation that leaves writing unchanged would be ambiguous between 'RSI content cannot be removed along one direction' and 'this direction is only a read-out at block 14'. The same write-up's head ablation shows the other half of the trap: probability fell on 318 of 477 steps, but the right token stayed first choice on 475.
transfers.concrete_measurement: For every direction that round 2 ablates or counter-steers (RSI axis, loop directions, foreign axes) fill two columns. Read: the held-out AUC with which the projection of the reader's mean block-14 state on the direction separates RSI texts from other texts (split by prompt, bootstrap interval). Use: the change that ablation and counter-steering cause in the writing-side outcomes (teacher-forced RSI-word log-probability, RSI projection of the read difference after generation, persona log-odds), set against two controls: for counter-steering a random direction at the same KL to the unpushed model, for ablation a control direction that carries the same variance of block-14 states. Add a re-emergence check: after ablation at block 14, the AUC of the same contrast read at blocks 16, 20 and 24. Reading rules, written down before the round-2 results are looked at: high AUC with a use effect no larger than the control's means detector, not mediator, and nothing follows about unlearning; high AUC with a use effect above the control and foreign effects inside the margin means mediator; an AUC that recovers at later blocks means the model rebuilds the content from other features. Report mean shifts and sign flips side by side.
transfers.cost: AUCs from stored reader states: minutes. The control-direction arm and later-block read-outs: about one extra arm per ablation condition.
transfers.risk: The round-2 plan is frozen, so the control arm and the re-emergence check are add-ons and must be labelled as outside the plan. A random direction removes almost no variance, which is why the ablation control has to be matched on variance and the steering control on KL; both matchings are approximate.

transfers.from: neuron_engineering: Synthetic Neuron Engineering of a Gemma 4 Coding Agent (Taneja); full paper read by the reader agent
transfers.idea: In Gemma 4 31B the 64 neurons that best predicted task success shared none with the 64 chosen by attribution patching to raise the log-probability of the correct fix. Scaling the predictive set did not help (57 of 88 attempts solved, 65 of 90 at baseline); the attribution-chosen set moved its target on held-out cases (20 of 25, random neurons 8 of 25). The support is weak, since the predictive signal was itself faint (held-out AUC 0.65, below the author's own bar of 0.70), so the measurement transfers, not the claim. The project's loop pushes the read direction (what the reader's block-14 mean shows) as if it were the use direction (what makes the writer produce RSI text). A mismatch would cost gain every round and would explain the round-1 decay differently from 'RSI content does not propagate'. The write-up also gives a yardstick: for a read-out with gradient g, the smallest change that moves it by c is c g / |g|^2; its conventional vector was 4 to 10 times (E2B) and 74 times (31B) longer.
transfers.concrete_measurement: On teacher-forced texts define a read-out R: mean logit of the RSI word set minus mean logit of a frequency-matched control set. Use direction g: the gradient of R with respect to the block-14 residual, summed over positions with each position weighted by its push size (the push is added at every position), averaged over half the prompts. (1) Efficiency eta(d) = cos(g, d) for the Euclidean-orthogonal RSI axis, each loop direction, the converged style direction and the foreign axes; 1/eta is the factor by which d needs more push norm than g for the same first-order change in R. (2) On the other half of the prompts push g, the read direction and a random direction at equal KL to the unpushed model; measure the change in R and the RSI projection of the read difference after one full write-and-read round. (3) Specific use direction: g for RSI with its components along the gradients of the sports, sea and tone read-outs removed, which is the smallest push that moves the RSI read-out while leaving the foreign ones unchanged to first order; test it on the replay set (item LM2) against the Euclidean-orthogonal axis. Criterion: mismatch is shown if eta of the read direction is small (below about 0.3) and the g push gives a larger read difference after generation at equal KL, with the random direction near zero; if both do alike, mismatch is ruled out.
transfers.cost: One backward pass per text on a few hundred texts, a KL calibration and one write-and-read round for three or four directions: a few GPU-hours.
transfers.risk: Gradient directions are local and can move a teacher-forced read-out without changing generated text; the write-up's own set closed 57% of its gap, flipped 6 of 25 cases and solved no more tasks. The read difference after free generation therefore decides. At the project's push sizes the first-order picture may not hold (item OT1 checks this). R inherits the weakness of small word sets (item OT2).

transfers.from: last_mile_copy: The Last Mile Is a Copy (Shree); full write-up read by the reader agent, figures and supplementary notebook not
transfers.idea: The write-up tests every repair on one fixed set of recorded moments (the prompt at an edit call plus what the model then wrote) and scores two rates on it: Rescue, the share of faulty moments that become correct, and Keep, the share of correct moments that stay correct. Its adapter rescued 56.6% against 10.9% for the unmodified model and kept 97.8% against 88.0%. The reader agent flags two weaknesses: the two arms are scored on different denominators (163 of 288 against 34 of 312), and the replay gain did not reach the end result (4 of 58 tasks, the same as baseline draws). The project's planned two-sided specificity criterion is this pair of rates under another name, and the outside probe (one teacher-forced run, no intervals, small word sets) needs exactly such a fixed, paired test bed before its finding can be believed or dismissed.
transfers.concrete_measurement: Freeze about 400 moments (a text prefix and its next-token position) from stored texts: 100 each from RSI, sports, sea and tone-marked texts, plus neutral ones for damage calibration. Run every push variant on the same moments: Euclidean-orthogonal RSI axis, lens-metric-orthogonal RSI axis, use direction (item NE1); each with both signs, additive and norm-preserving, all set to the same KL to the unpushed model on the neutral moments. Per moment record the target effect (change in log-probability of a stratum's own word set when its axis is counter-steered, the analogue of Rescue) and the foreign effects (change of every other stratum's word set on that stratum's moments, the analogue of Keep). A variant passes if the target effect exceeds a preset size and every foreign effect lies inside the preset margin, with intervals from a sign-flip test paired by moment and clustered by source text, on identical moments for all variants. The outside finding is confirmed if, for the Euclidean-orthogonal axis, the foreign effects exclude zero with one sign across the three foreign sets; it is explained if they vanish for the lens-metric-orthogonal axis. Every passing variant then gets one free-generation write-and-read round as confirmation.
transfers.cost: Half a day to build and freeze the set. Each variant is about a thousand forward passes, so a dozen variants take well under one GPU-hour; one generation round per passing variant on top.
transfers.risk: A teacher-forced replay effect may not appear in free generation, as in the write-up. A stratified set is enriched, so its rates are not base rates. Equal KL on neutral moments does not guarantee equal damage on the strata.

transfers.from: one_tensor: Fixing Gemma's Copying Errors by Changing One Tensor (Yamamoto); read through the author's evidence repository only, the paper text was not read
transfers.idea: The write-up's strongest evidence is a dose series on the suspect tensor that includes a worsening dose. With multipliers 0.25, 1, 2 and 4 and above, the correct token is first choice in 0, 1, 10 and 10 of 10 contexts (median probability 0.0000, 0.0297, 0.9997, 1.0000), with perplexity as the harm check (72.85, 61.57, 60.57, about 60.55) and a partial reversal in the healthy model. The reader agent notes one gap: the 'gain' was computed from stored weights and never measured during generation. Both points carry over. A monotone dose series gives the positive control, which failed narrowly in round 1, a second way to pass that does not hang on one contrast. And the project's planned Jacobian quantities are computed gains too, valid only for small pushes, while the loop uses pushes proportional to the residual norm.
transfers.concrete_measurement: Positive control as a series: push a direction with a known answer (the instructed RSI axis, and a foreign axis such as sports whose word set is unambiguous) at 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 times the standard alpha, pro and anti. Read (a) the teacher-forced change in log-probability of the matching word set, (b) the projection of the read difference on the pushed axis after one write-and-read round, (c) KL to the unpushed model. Test the per-prompt slope of (a) and (b) on the realised dose (mean push norm over residual norm, since the clamp at twice the median norm and the later normalisation make alpha a poor dose axis) with a sign-flip test clustered by prompt, restricted to doses under a preset KL bound. Pass criterion: slope interval above zero, dose means in monotone order, sign reversal between pro and anti. Linear-regime check: at each dose compare the measured change (a) with the first-order prediction from the J-lens; report the dose at which the relative error passes 25% and whether the standard round-1 push lies below it. If it does not, lambda_RSI, the lens-metric orthogonalisation and gradient-based use directions describe smaller pushes than the loop applies.
transfers.cost: Four doses times two axes times one write-and-read round, about 8 times one positive-control run, plus teacher-forced passes: a few GPU-hours.
transfers.risk: At high dose damage bends the curve (the write-up's read-out saturates from the doubled tensor on), so a slope fitted over the full range misleads; the KL bound handles this but costs power. If the instructed axis still fails as a series, the reader, not the null, is at fault, which is itself a result. The write-up's own series rests on 10 hand-picked contexts.

transfers.from: one_tensor: Fixing Gemma's Copying Errors by Changing One Tensor (Yamamoto); read through the author's evidence repository only, the paper text was not read
transfers.idea: The write-up does not use a hand-picked word list. It takes a census of all 432 names whose tokenisation ends in a lone 's' token and compares them with 7,224 other names from the same source as a within-set control (260 of 432 failures against 8 of 7,224), then repeats the split on plurals and code blocks. The stratum is defined by tokenisation, which turned out to be the variable that mattered. The reader agent lists as a gap that no random, non-enriched sample was tested. The project's outside probe (pushing against the Euclidean-orthogonal RSI axis raises the log-probability of sports, sea and tone words) rests on small hand-made word sets without a control stratum. It cannot yet separate 'the foreign axes are disturbed' from 'frequent concrete words in general go up when an abstract direction is pushed down'.
transfers.concrete_measurement: Build each word set as a census from a fixed outside source (for example every noun of a category list), at least 50 words per set. Split each set by tokenisation: single-token words (with leading space) and multi-token words, the latter scored by first token and by whole-word log-probability separately. Add two control strata: vocabulary words matched to each set in unigram frequency, and concrete nouns unrelated to any axis. On the replay set (item LM2) compute per stratum the change in mean log-probability when pushing with and against the RSI axis at equal KL. Criterion: the outside finding is specific only if the foreign-set change exceeds the change of both control strata, with a prompt-clustered interval excluding zero and the same sign in the single-token and multi-token strata. Use the same census for the RSI-word subspace of the planned lambda_RSI iteration, and report lambda_RSI beside the same gain for a frequency-matched control subspace of equal size.
transfers.cost: Word-list preparation: a few hours. Scoring is part of the replay-set runs, minutes of GPU.
transfers.risk: A census brings in rare and ambiguous words (bank, wave) that add noise, and frequency matching is approximate. Large sets can dilute an effect carried by a few central words, so the per-word distribution has to be reported beside the mean.

transfers.from: latent_roadmaps: Latent Roadmaps, Soft-Token Re-Feeding in DiffusionGemma for Code Graphs (UncleBumblebeer); full write-up read by the reader agent, linked repositories not opened. The link to the project is loose.
transfers.idea: The write-up's central contrast is one pass against a chain of passes with the same weights, and its exact-match scores show drift along the chain (47.8% after two chained steps and 0.0% after three, on different task sets, while the lenient 22-way score stays at 82.1% and 90.8%). It has no arm that feeds the true intermediate state, so one-step error and accumulated drift are not separated. The project can make that separation cheaply, and this is my extension, not something the write-up does: if every round restarts from the same prompts, as the loop description implies, the loop is the repeated application of one map from pushed direction to read direction. That map can be estimated from single rounds, composed, and compared with the observed loops.
transfers.concrete_measurement: From round-1 data collect all pairs (pushed direction, unnormalised read difference) over all loops and rounds. The pushed directions are known exactly, so fit a linear map M by least squares on their span (a dynamic mode decomposition). Leave-one-loop-out test: fit on the other loops and predict the held-out loop's RSI share and gain round by round by iterating unit(M d). Report the eigenvalues of M, the cosine of the dominant mode with the shared style direction, and, for the mode with the largest RSI-axis content, its eigenvalue relative to the largest (the through-text counterpart of lambda_RSI against the largest gain overall). One new arm tests additivity: push the normalised sum of the RSI axis and the style direction and compare the read difference with the sum of the two separate ones. Reading rules: if held-out trajectories are predicted within the replicate spread (item SN2), the round-1 decay is the spectrum of one linear map and the RSI question reduces to one eigenvalue ratio; a ratio near 1 would justify a deflated loop in round 1b (style mode projected out each round); if prediction fails, the loop is nonlinear or noise-driven and Jacobian-based gains will not describe it.
transfers.cost: Analysis of stored round-1 directions: CPU minutes. The additivity arm is one write-and-read round.
transfers.risk: Few loops and rounds give few pairs, and they cluster near the style direction once loops converge, so the fit is well determined only for early rounds; the eigenvalue of a weak RSI mode is the least certain number. Noise in the read differences inflates the apparent rank.

transfers.from: last_mile_copy: The Last Mile Is a Copy (Shree); full write-up read by the reader agent, figures and supplementary notebook not
transfers.idea: The write-up feeds recorded outputs back token by token and reads every layer with a logit-lens-style read-out. On wrong steps the token that is eventually written first leads at layer 35 (median), against layer 31 on correct steps, and in 42 of 146 wrong steps the right token leads somewhere in layers 28 to 40 and is then overtaken. A preference can be present mid-stack and lost late. The project pushes at block 14 and looks only at the output and at the reader. Whether pushed RSI content survives the later blocks or is overtaken there is not measured, and it is something the two lenses of round 1b can show.
transfers.concrete_measurement: Teacher-forced on the replay set (item LM2), for each block from 14 to the last, read with the logit lens and with the J-lens the quantity S: the change (pushed minus unpushed) in mean log-probability of the RSI word set minus that of the frequency-matched control set; the same for a set of style markers and for the foreign sets. Compute the profile over blocks for pushes with and against the RSI axis, a loop direction, the converged style direction and a random direction, all at equal KL to the unpushed model. Criterion: RSI content is 'overtaken' if S for the RSI set peaks at an intermediate block and loses more than half of the peak by the last block, with an interval over prompts, while the style profile holds or rises; it is 'carried through' if the profile does not fall. Also report the share of positions at which an RSI-set token leads at some block but not at the output. An overtaken profile names the blocks to open with the expert-filtered J++ lens and argues for testing a later injection block.
transfers.cost: Hooks at every block on a few hundred moments. The logit lens is negligible; the J-lens adds its usual cost once per block, a few GPU-hours at most.
transfers.risk: The logit lens is unreliable in middle blocks, so the profile counts only where both lenses agree in shape. A falling profile is correlational; the write-up had no causal test of its 'overtaken' cases either.

transfers.from: last_mile_copy: The Last Mile Is a Copy (Shree); full write-up read by the reader agent, figures and supplementary notebook not
transfers.idea: In the write-up wrong copies were not sampling accidents: the first wrong token was the model's first choice in 145 of 146 cases, with probability at least 0.9 in 143, and exact copies on those moments were 11.9%, 11.5% and 8.7% at temperatures 0, 0.25 and 1.0. Temperature could not matter because the loss was already in the logits. Round 2's temperature and gain phase diagram assumes that sampling temperature modulates what the loop carries. Whether it can do so for RSI content is checkable from the writer's logits, and the answer changes how a flat or a steep diagram should be read.
transfers.concrete_measurement: From stored logits of the pushed and the unpushed writer along the same texts: per position, the push-induced change of probability mass on the RSI word set, binned by the unpushed first-choice probability (below 0.5, 0.5 to 0.9, above 0.9). Then, for every temperature of the round-2 grid, the expected number of RSI-set tokens per text, obtained by rescaling the stored logits (near temperature zero only positions where the push changes the first choice count). Compare this predicted temperature dependence with the observed RSI projection of the read difference per cell of the phase diagram. Reading rules: if the prediction is flat, a flat diagram means the loss sits in the logits, not in sampling; if RSI mass shifts mostly at uncertain positions, a threshold in push size is expected at low temperature (first choices must flip) and the phase boundary should bend accordingly; if the observed dependence is much stronger than predicted, temperature acts through style and damage, not through RSI content.
transfers.cost: Storing logits (or the top-50 probabilities) for a few hundred continuations during round 2, then CPU analysis: negligible, but the storing has to be switched on before the run.
transfers.risk: The prediction is first order: it keeps the prefixes sampled at the reference temperature, whereas real texts diverge as temperature changes. A small RSI word set misses paraphrased content, so 'no RSI mass' can be a word-list artefact.

transfers.from: neuron_engineering: Synthetic Neuron Engineering of a Gemma 4 Coding Agent (Taneja); full paper read by the reader agent
transfers.idea: Two details of the write-up's statistics bear on the corrected null planned for round 1b. Its null for the predictive neurons repeats the whole selection 200 times on labels shuffled within tasks, so the null includes the selection step. And its main result is significant by case (20 of 25, p = 0.004) but not by task (9 of 12, p = 0.15), because cases from one task are not independent. Round 1's positive control failed narrowly because its null was conservative, so the replacement should be validated before it is trusted, in both directions.
transfers.concrete_measurement: Paired sign-flip test with the prompt as the unit: all continuations of one prompt flip together. Inside every flip recompute the whole pipeline that yields the statistic (mean difference, centring, orthogonalisation against the foreign axes in the chosen metric, normalisation, and any selection of layer, word set or lens filter), then the statistic itself (cosine with the RSI axis, lambda_RSI, the specificity ratio); at least 2,000 flips. Fit axes and lens metric on one half of the prompts and test on the other. Validate the null twice before use: on A/A data (two halves of one condition labelled pro and anti) the rejection rate at the 5% level should be near 5%, neither far below (conservative, the round-1 failure) nor above; on the stored round-1 positive-control data the test should now pass. Report by-prompt p-values as primary and by-text ones as secondary only.
transfers.cost: Analysis only, on stored per-text states: minutes to an hour of CPU.
transfers.risk: With few prompts the by-prompt test has little power (the write-up's p went from 0.004 to 0.15), and the remedy is more prompts, not more continuations per prompt. Flipping only the loop data treats the axes as fixed and ignores their own estimation noise unless they are cross-fitted or bootstrapped.

transfers.from: signal_noise: Signal and Noise in a Budget-Limited Coding Agent (Almarwani); full write-up read. The write-up supplies only the noise-floor framing; the model below is my own derivation.
transfers.idea: The write-up's noise arithmetic (a difference inside the rerun spread is not an effect; the number of run pairs needed grows with noise squared over effect squared) can be carried into the loop's dynamics. This step is my own derivation and should be checked. Each round re-estimates the direction from finitely many sampled texts and renormalises it. In a linear loop with Gaussian sampling noise a mode therefore survives only if its one-step response (norm g alpha when pushed alone) exceeds the norm tau of the sampling error: the stationary squared alignment with the dominant mode is 1 - tau^2 / (g alpha)^2 above that threshold and zero below it. A weaker mode such as RSI loses ground to the dominant one by the ratio of the two gains per round until it reaches the noise floor. This would make the round-2 phase boundary a statement about signal against sampling noise.
transfers.concrete_measurement: Toy: simulate d_next = unit(M d + noise) in the model's dimension with two modes (style gain g_S, RSI gain g_R below it) and noise of total variance tau^2; map alignment and RSI share over g_S alpha / tau and g_R / g_S. Use it as the null model beside the backprop and predictive-coding toys. Three checks against data: (1) with tau and |m| from item SN2, the cosine between independently run, converged round-1 loops should equal the single-round reliability r; (2) in round 2, estimate response and tau per temperature and gain cell and test whether all cells fall on one curve when alignment is plotted against response over tau, with the boundary at 1; (3) from single-round pushes of the RSI axis and of the style direction, the predicted per-round shrink factor of the RSI-to-style ratio should match the observed round-1 decay. Criterion: if the three checks hold within the replicate spread, the loop is a noisy power iteration and the round-1 decay needs no RSI-specific explanation; a failed check shows where the nonlinear or RSI-specific part lies.
transfers.cost: Minutes of CPU for the toy; the checks reuse quantities from item SN2 and round 2, plus a bootstrap per cell.
transfers.risk: The assumptions are crude: one dominant mode, noise independent of the pushed direction, a response linear in the push. The clamp in the push and the normalisation layers make the gain depend on direction and size. A toy with two free gains fits many curves, so only the three out-of-sample checks count.

transfers.from: signal_noise: Signal and Noise in a Budget-Limited Coding Agent (Almarwani); full write-up read by the reader agent
transfers.idea: The author checked that all 814 model requests really reached the adapter, and found that a tool declared in 811 traced attempts was never called in any of 1,261. The rest of the write-up (leaderboard variance figures, task-difficulty strata, harness labelling pitfalls) is specific to the competition and does not transfer. The check does: the project's push has a clamp and runs inside cached generation, and whether it acts as specified on every token should be recorded, not assumed.
transfers.concrete_measurement: During every writing run log per generated token the realised push norm divided by the residual norm, the share of tokens at which the clamp at twice the median norm is active, and the number of hook calls per generated token. Assert that the reader runs with no hook attached and averages continuation tokens only. Compare the logged dose with the nominal alpha for each cell of the round-2 grid, and flag any cell whose realised dose deviates from nominal by more than about 10% before its result is interpreted.
transfers.cost: A few lines of logging, no extra compute; it has to be switched on before round 2 runs.
transfers.risk: None of substance. Without the log, a difference between cells cannot be separated from a difference in realised dose.

transfers.from: one_tensor: Fixing Gemma's Copying Errors by Changing One Tensor (Yamamoto); read through the author's evidence repository only, the paper text was not read
transfers.idea: The finding itself does not transfer. One projection tensor is about 65 times too small in the quantised Gemma 4 E4B release, so the RMSNorm epsilon (1e-6) stops being negligible against a mean square near 8e-7; doubling the tensor, or a rank-128 SVD adapter, repairs dropped final 's' tokens (268 to 1 failures on 7,688 selected names). This is a release defect in one checkpoint. The project's block-14 residual stream should be many orders of magnitude above any norm epsilon, and the project changes activations, not weights, so the write-up is no evidence that normalisation layers distort pushes, and the closed-form adapter has no use here. The user's note mentions 'not a proven mantissa error'; the reader agent did not find that phrase in the repository, so it stays unverified and is not used.
transfers.concrete_measurement: None, apart from a one-off check: confirm that the mean square of the block-14 residual, and of pre-norm activations in the toy networks, is far above the norm epsilon, and, if a converted or quantised Qwen3 checkpoint is used, that its per-tensor RMS matches the reference weights.
transfers.risk: Over-reading the analogy. The only place the epsilon effect could plausibly bite is a toy network with very small activations.

transfers.from: latent_roadmaps: Latent Roadmaps, Soft-Token Re-Feeding in DiffusionGemma for Code Graphs (UncleBumblebeer); full write-up read by the reader agent, linked repositories not opened
transfers.idea: The headline does not bear on whether RSI content can sustain itself through text. The rise from 48.0% to 82.1% comes from a model adapted by LoRA for exactly the re-fed format; the caller supplies every step; the one-pass arm receives an unfactored compound prompt; the from-scratch and autoregressive baselines gain from re-feeding too (34.6% and 55.0%); and nothing passes through tokens. In an autoregressive loop a push at block 14 can come back to block 14 only through emitted tokens, so there is no latent return path to study. The literal counterpart, a reader fed the writer's probability-weighted mix of input embeddings in place of sampled tokens, is feasible but low value: such inputs are off-distribution, the write-up's own off-distribution arm stayed at the floor (26.4% against a floor of 25.0%), and a null would say nothing. Consider it only if item LM4 shows the RSI probability shift mainly at uncertain positions.
transfers.concrete_measurement: None recommended now. For the toy comparison of backprop and predictive coding the write-up gives one caution only: its autoregressive comparison had 7% of the training steps and one seed and could not be interpreted, so match the two toy networks on held-out loss and number of seeds before comparing their loops.
transfers.risk: Reading 're-feeding helps' as support for self-sustaining loops would be a forced analogy.

transfers.from: neuron_engineering: Synthetic Neuron Engineering of a Gemma 4 Coding Agent (Taneja); full paper read by the reader agent
transfers.idea: Neuron transplants between model sizes through ridge maps, engineered and gated neurons, imitation of a larger model's tool choices and the packaging of weight edits as LoRA adapters do not transfer: the project has one model, acts on activations and has no agent task. Weight-level direction removal is not a new option for round 2 either: applied to every component that writes into the residual stream up to block 14, it equals the residual-stream projection already planned. One cautionary result is worth remembering when round 2 is read: loop removal suppressed its target on E2B (2 of 48 reruns loop again, against 12 with a random direction and 15 at baseline) without more tasks solved, and the same recipe rebuilt for 12B more than halved them (7 against 16 of 40). Suppressing a read-out is not changing behaviour, and the side effects showed only end to end.
transfers.risk: None beyond over-reading; the author states that no intervention raised the number of tasks solved.

transfers.from: last_mile_copy: The Last Mile Is a Copy (Shree); full write-up read by the reader agent, figures and supplementary notebook not
transfers.idea: The copy-specific content does not transfer: the four attention heads that attend to the source position, the copy adapter, the tool-side snap repair, plain-text tool outputs and the parser hang all concern exact copying of a visible span. The write-up gives no reason to hunt for 'RSI heads': its own four heads appear to have been chosen and evaluated on overlapping data, and with all four switched off the right token remained first choice on 475 of 477 steps.

summary:
None of the five write-ups says anything about RSI loops or Qwen3, and none of their headline results transfers as evidence. What transfers is a set of measurement designs and cautionary cases: 14 items, plus four explicit 'not transferable' entries. All five sources were located and read by the reader agents (one_tensor only through the author's repository, not the paper), so no item rests on an unverified note; the note's phrase 'not a proven mantissa error' could not be verified and is not used.

Highest value, in order:
1. SN1: which tokens carry the reader's mean. In signal_noise 85.1% of a held-out gain sat in 20.8% of the tokens.
2. SN2: seed-replicate noise floor, reliability-corrected RSI share, margins for null claims.
3. NE2: how much of an in-context persona effect passes through block 14 at all. This decides whether round 1's behavioural null is informative.
4. LM1: detector-or-mediator reading rules for the round-2 ablation.
5. NE1: read direction against use direction, with an efficiency number and a first-order specific push.
6. LM2: frozen replay set with paired two-sided scoring, the test bed for the outside probe's finding.

By write-up:
- one_tensor: a dose series for the positive control (OT1) and census-built word sets with control strata (OT2). The tensor defect and its fix do not transfer.
- latent_roadmaps: only a loosely linked composition test of the measured one-step map (LR1). Latent re-feeding itself does not transfer, because an autoregressive loop has no latent return path.
- neuron_engineering: NE1, NE2 and details for the corrected null (NE3). Transplants and weight edits do not transfer.
- last_mile_copy: LM1, LM2, a layer profile of pushed content (LM3) and a temperature reading aid (LM4). Copy heads and the adapter do not transfer.
- signal_noise: SN1, SN2, a push log (SN4) and, as my own extension, a noise-threshold toy model (SN3).

Timing: four things have to be fixed or switched on before round 2 runs, without changing its frozen plan: the LM1 reading rules and control arm, seed replicates and the contrast family (SN2), logit storage (LM4) and the push log (SN4).

Common caution: three of the write-ups (neuron_engineering, last_mile_copy, signal_noise) show a teacher-forced or likelihood proxy moving while the end result does not, so every item ends in a free-generation check. All five are single-team, mostly single-run hackathon reports on Gemma 4 coding agents. SN3 and LR1 go beyond what their write-ups do and are marked as such.

verdicts.reasoning: The source supports this only as a statistical caution. The write-up's split was made post hoc on 10 rows and says nothing about this model. The concern still applies directly: a mean can be carried by a token class that is not the one you care about, and this reader averages every continuation token. The plan does not cover it, it is cheap, and it could change how both round-1 findings are read. Two flaws would mislead as written. (1) Per-class shares of a sum centred on the grand mean depend on the centring point. A class that is merely more frequent in one arm (more list markers, longer texts) gets a share that moves with the reference, so composition effects must be separated from within-class shifts. (2) The placeholder re-read changes later states through attention. Excluding positions from the average is the cleaner first test. The RSI list is also the small hand-made list that OT2 criticises, so a small class-1 share would not show that the RSI share is non-lexical. The class most likely to dominate an unclamped mean is missing: high-norm (massive-activation) tokens, which the push itself clamps.
verdicts.changed_measurement: Use an exact two-way split per class k and axis a: m.a = sum_k (w_k^pro - w_k^anti)(mubar_k - c).a [composition] + sum_k wbar_k (mu_k^pro - mu_k^anti).a [within]. Here w_k is the arm's mean per-text share of class-k tokens, mu_k is the arm's class mean (text-weighted as in the reader), bars are two-arm averages and c is the pooled token mean. Write the convention down before the re-read. Report both terms per class and round with prompt-bootstrap intervals, and split |m|^2 (the denominator of the RSI share) the same way. Fix the classes in advance: the five proposed, plus tokens whose block-14 norm exceeds twice the median (the push's clamp threshold), think-block tokens if Qwen3 thinking was on, and position bins. Counterfactuals: first drop the RSI-list positions from the average (no text edit), then do the placeholder re-read; the gap between the two is how far the keywords spread through context. Class 1 uses OT2's census list. Reading: a style direction carried by composition terms of the format or high-norm classes is a layout attractor; an RSI share carried by class-1 within terms, and lost when those positions are excluded, is lexical.

verdicts.reasoning: The point is sound and does not depend on the coding-agent setting. Each direction is a finite-sample mean difference, so |m| has a positive floor and cosines with fixed axes are attenuated. That bears directly on whether the round-1 RSI decay is real. (The phrase 'no detectable change' is the reader agent's, not the author's; this does not matter.) Three parts would mislead as written. Holm correction over all phase-diagram cells leaves no cell standing and turns the diagram into a power failure. Margins for round-1 null claims set now are post hoc unless tied to an independent scale. The reliability correction assumes isotropic noise, but text-sampling noise at block 14 sits mostly in a few high-variance style and format directions. The correction is therefore least trustworthy exactly along the style direction, and isotropic formulas cannot tell noise-driven convergence from gain-driven convergence (see SN3).
verdicts.changed_measurement: (a) As proposed, with splits by prompt; report 'not resolvable' below r = 0.2. (b) Add one null run before round 2: both arms unpushed (alpha = 0), on the same prompts and with the sample sizes of a round-2 cell. It gives tau^2 and the noise covariance directly (its top principal directions and their cosine with the converged style direction). It also serves as the A/A set for NE3 and the noise model for SN3. (c) Seed replicates as proposed, plus one same-seed rerun to measure numerical nondeterminism. (d) Replace Holm over cells with at most five structural contrasts named in advance, Holm over those only. Examples: trend of the RSI share along temperature at fixed gain, and along gain at fixed temperature; boundary location against the SN3 prediction; counter-steering against the foreign-axis control. (e) Express equivalence margins as fractions of an independent effect: persona log-odds against a set share of the instruction effect G (NE2); foreign effects against a set share of the same push's target effect. (f) Before round 2, use round-1 per-prompt variance to compute how many prompts the smallest effect of interest needs. Check that the smallest attainable sign-flip p, 2^(1-P) for P prompts, is below 0.05/k for k contrasts: P >= 10 for k = 20, P >= 8 for k = 5.

verdicts.reasoning: Support from the source is weak. The weight-written sentence was one run, inside the noise: 147 and 135, against 141 unchanged and 163 for the control, while the in-context arm's no-sentence baseline was 153. It was also a fitted rank-128 weight edit, so its failure may come from poor generalisation of the fit rather than from depth. The measurement stands anyway: activation patching is the cheapest way to learn whether the round-1 behavioural null says anything. Patching only the positions after the instruction correctly leaves later layers free to read the neutral instruction, so (1) is the on-distribution ceiling for an intervention at those positions. But the block profile (3) rises with depth almost by construction, because the instruction's information moves onto later positions as depth increases. Choosing the injection block from it therefore favours late blocks, ignores that the reader also sits at block 14, and leaves less computation before the output. A step between whole-state patching and a constant push is missing, and G itself has not been checked as a sensitivity gate.
verdicts.changed_measurement: Step 0, before round 2: compute G per statement with prompt-bootstrap intervals. If the instruction effect is small or its sign is inconsistent, demote persona log-odds to a secondary endpoint. Then: (1) whole-state patch at block 14 on the positions after the instruction; (1b) rank-1 patch, replacing only the component along the instruction direction u with the instructed run's per-position values; (2) constant push of u at the standard push size; (2b) the rank-1 patch along the RSI axis, a round-1 loop direction and the style direction. verdicts.reasoning: The derivation holds under its assumptions. With a rank-one response g alpha and isotropic noise of total variance tau^2, the fixed point of the squared alignment is 1 - tau^2/(g alpha)^2, and zero below the threshold. Text-to-text variability at block 14 is anisotropic, so a weak or noise-dominated loop drifts toward the top principal directions of the noise, and those could be the 'shared style direction'. A noise attractor gives read differences whose sign is random across loops and rounds; a gain mode gives a consistent sign. With two free gains the toy can fit many curves, so it should be parameterised with measured quantities.

summary:
None of the write-ups gives evidence about RSI loops. Every item kept is a measurement design whose value rests on the project's own logic. Several duplicate planned work and are merged: NE1 into the planned RSI-restricted use direction, NE3 into the planned sign-flip null, OT2 into LM2, LM3 into OT1, and LR1 with SN3. 16 entries are kept with changes; OT0 and LM0 are dropped.

Fixes that prevent wrong conclusions:
- SN1: class shares centred on the grand mean depend on the reference point, so composition must be split from within-class shifts.
- LM1: the read AUC saturates, and the reader-side re-emergence check shows recovery by construction.
- LM2/OT2: the outside probe's geometric and teacher-forced findings are largely one first-order fact, so word sets must be cross-fitted and control strata added.
- NE3: the null must not be validated by making the positive control pass.
- SN2: no Holm correction across phase-diagram cells.
- SN3: the isotropic-noise model hides a noise-attractor explanation of the style convergence; test the sign.
- NE0: the claimed equivalence between weight-level and single-site ablation is false.

Before round 2, without changing the frozen plan:

- storage of per-token reader states and top-50 log-probabilities;
- one alpha = 0 null run (A/A data for NE3, tau and the noise covariance for SN2 and SN3);
- a power and prompt-count check against a small contrast family named in advance;
- written LM1 and NE0 reading rules, with mean-ablation;
- NE2 step 0: is the persona read-out sensitive at all?
